subject: Day 1: Start where you are
title: Five psalms, three thank-yous, one simple beginning.
body:
Good morning.

Your journey begins with wisdom, struggle, prayer, and trust. The Psalms make room for real life from the very first pages.

Read all five together or spread them throughout your day. Then begin your gratitude list.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Something that grounds you, someone who supports you, and a small gift from today.

subject: Day 2: Bring your whole heart
title: Wonder and worry can belong in the same prayer.
body:
Good morning.

Today's readings move between distress, wonder, praise, and hard questions. You don't need to settle every feeling before giving thanks.

Notice which psalm sounds most like your life today.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Beauty you noticed, kindness you received, and something that brought comfort.

subject: Day 3: Thankful while you're still waiting
title: Your unfinished prayers have a place here.
body:
Good morning.

"How long?" belongs in the language of faith. These psalms give us words for waiting and longing for things to be made right.

Let your gratitude be honest and specific today.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Someone you can trust, a word that steadied you, and a good thing present in the waiting.

subject: Day 4: Look up for a moment
title: Let today's reading draw your attention outward.
body:
Good morning.

These psalms include refuge, rescue, creation, and prayer for help. Psalm 19 invites you to notice what the heavens declare.

Take a brief pause outdoors or by a window before writing today's list.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Something beautiful, something dependable, and help you've received.

subject: Day 5: Gratitude in the valley
title: You can give thanks without pretending the road is easy.
body:
Good morning.

Today's readings include deep anguish and the shepherd's care. Both belong in the Psalms; both may belong in your story.

As you read, notice words you can carry into your own prayers.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Care you've received, a place of rest, and guidance for a next step.

subject: Day 6: Remember a lighter moment
title: Make room for the joy you've known.
body:
Good morning.

Today's psalms include seeking God, asking for help, and celebrating relief.

Think back to a moment when tension eased or joy returned. Write down enough detail to remember it later.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: A burden lightened, a prayer you could speak, and a moment that made you smile.

subject: Day 7: A week of noticing
title: Pause and read what you've already written.
body:
Good morning.

Refuge, forgiveness, praise, and trouble all appear in today's readings. Gratitude grows within this full, complicated life.

You've reached your first week. Look back at your list and notice the people and gifts that keep appearing.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: A fresh start, a kindness, and a source of encouragement.

subject: Day 8: The good that takes time
title: Notice what has grown slowly.
body:
Good morning.

Today's readings invite trust and patience while giving voice to weakness and need. Psalm 40 remembers waiting for help.

Consider something good in your life that developed gradually.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Someone patient, something you've learned over time, and support you received along the way.

subject: Day 9: When your heart needs a reminder
title: Let remembering become part of your prayer.
body:
Good morning.

These psalms include longing, sorrow, communal grief, and celebration. In Psalms 42-43, the speaker repeatedly turns a troubled heart toward hope.

Today, remember goodness you can name without dismissing what feels hard.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: A comforting memory, a present kindness, and something that helps you hope.

subject: Day 10: A quiet place in a busy month
title: Take one unhurried breath before you begin.
body:
Good morning.

Today's readings speak of refuge, worship, mortality, and thanksgiving. They invite us to consider what deserves our trust and attention.

Find a quiet moment—even a brief one—to read and respond.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: A place to pause, something of lasting value, and an everyday provision.

subject: Day 11: Thankful for another beginning
title: Mercy gives us something worth remembering.
body:
Good morning.

Repentance, betrayal, danger, and pleas for help run through these psalms. Psalm 51 offers language for an honest return to God.

Think of the patience and mercy that have made new beginnings possible in your life.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Forgiveness received, a lesson learned, and someone who has been patient with you.

subject: Day 12: A thank-you for steady support
title: Remember what helped when you felt afraid.
body:
Good morning.

These are prayers from places of pressure and conflict. Their trust does not depend on ignoring danger.

You may not share every circumstance, but you may recognize the need for help.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Someone who reassured you, practical help you received, and a moment of courage.

subject: Day 13: What restores you?
title: Notice where you've found rest and nourishment.
body:
Good morning.

Today's readings move through refuge, thirst for God, protection, and the abundance of a watered earth.

Pay attention to what restores you when you feel worn down.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Something that refreshes you, something that nourishes you, and somewhere you can rest.

subject: Day 14: Remember—and reach outward
title: Gratitude can help us notice other people's needs.
body:
Good morning.

Praise and pleas for rescue sit close together today. Psalm 67 looks outward, asking that God's ways become known among the nations.

As you give thanks, remember goodness that reaches beyond your own household.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Someone serving others, a shared resource, and a kindness that crossed a boundary.

subject: Day 15: Halfway through, with more to notice
title: Your list is becoming a record of this season.
body:
Good morning.

These psalms wrestle with aging, justice, envy, and loss. They invite a longer view of faithfulness.

You're halfway through the month. Read a few earlier gratitude entries before adding today's three.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Support across the years, wisdom from someone else, and a gift you might otherwise have forgotten.

subject: Day 16: Borrow a little courage from memory
title: Look back at what helped carry you.
body:
Good morning.

Remembering plays an important role in these readings, especially when the present is painful or uncertain.

Today, think about the stories that remind you help and goodness have been real in your life.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: A remembered kindness, a story that strengthens you, and someone who helped you through.

subject: Day 17: Thankful for a place to belong
title: Remember where you've been welcomed.
body:
Good morning.

Today's readings include calls to listen, cries for justice, longing for God's dwelling, and prayer for restoration.

Psalm 84 gives particular voice to the desire to be near God.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: A welcoming place, a person who makes room for you, and a moment of peace.

subject: Day 18: When the reading feels heavy
title: You don't have to force a cheerful ending.
body:
Good morning.

Some of today's words are difficult. Psalm 88 ends in darkness; Psalm 90 reflects on life's brevity.

Let these prayers make room for honesty. Your gratitude can be small and quiet today.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: A gentle comfort, someone safe to turn to, and one moment you're glad you had.

subject: Day 19: Begin with this morning
title: Give an ordinary part of the day your attention.
body:
Good morning.

These readings turn our attention toward refuge, praise, justice, and worship. Psalm 92 connects thanksgiving with the rhythms of morning and night.

Try noticing one gift at the beginning, middle, and end of your day.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: A morning gift, an afternoon kindness, and an evening comfort.

subject: Day 20: Let yourself celebrate
title: There's plenty of room for joy today.
body:
Good morning.

Today's readings overflow with invitations to sing and give thanks. Creation itself joins the celebration.

Let your list include delight: music, laughter, good news, or a simple pleasure you love.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Something joyful, something beautiful, and something worth celebrating with another person.

subject: Day 21: Remember the gifts you live on
title: Familiar blessings still deserve a place on your list.
body:
Good morning.

Today's readings include personal commitments, suffering, mercy, creation, and remembered history.

Psalms 103-105 offer many reasons to pause and give thanks. Notice which ones connect with your own life.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Care for your daily needs, mercy you've received, and a memory of help.

subject: Day 22: Your story can hold a thank-you
title: Remember a turning point.
body:
Good morning.

These psalms include failure, rescue, praise, and fierce conflict. Psalm 107 gathers several stories of people crying out and receiving help.

Think of a moment when your own circumstances changed or someone helped you move forward.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Help in difficulty, an unexpected kindness, and a turning point you're grateful for.

subject: Day 23: Small details, lasting gratitude
title: Give today's thank-yous a little more detail.
body:
Good morning.

Today's readings celebrate God's works, compassion, deliverance, and faithfulness.

Make your gratitude entries specific enough to become memories. Instead of "my friend," write what your friend did and why it mattered.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: A thoughtful action, an everyday provision, and something that inspired awe.

subject: Day 24: Give today's longer reading some room
title: Psalm 119 makes this a good day to read in portions.
body:
Good morning.

Today includes Psalm 119, the longest psalm. Consider splitting the reading between morning, midday, and evening, or listening to it.

Notice the repeated desire for guidance, understanding, and help.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Wise guidance, something you're learning, and words that have encouraged you.

subject: Day 25: Gratitude for the road you've traveled
title: Remember who helped you along the way.
body:
Good morning.

These short Songs of Ascents include prayers for help, peace, mercy, and protection.

Think about a journey in your own life—a literal trip or a season of change—and the care you received along it.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: A companion, help along the way, and a place that welcomed you.

subject: Day 26: What you would bring to the table
title: Choose a gratitude story worth sharing.
body:
Good morning.

Today's psalms make room for joy, work, family, hardship, and waiting. These are also the things we often carry into gatherings.

Choose one entry from your list to share with someone. Add the story behind it.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: A shared joy, someone you cherish, and a hope that sustains you.

subject: Day 27: A quieter kind of gratitude
title: Today's thanks can be simple and unhurried.
body:
Good morning.

Psalm 131 offers an image of a quieted soul. The readings that follow include worship, unity, and remembrance.

Before writing, take a moment to settle. Which good things become easier to notice when you slow down?

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: A peaceful moment, a connection with someone, and a familiar comfort.

subject: Day 28: Bring both joy and sorrow
title: The Psalms leave room for your whole experience.
body:
Good morning.

Today places enduring love beside the grief and anger of exile, thanksgiving beside danger.

If a passage unsettles you, you can acknowledge that in prayer. Let your gratitude be equally honest.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: A kindness that has lasted, someone who knows you well, and comfort during a hard time.

subject: Day 29: Who helped you keep going?
title: Remember the support behind your next step.
body:
Good morning.

These readings move through pleas for protection and guidance toward the generous praise of Psalm 145.

As the challenge nears its end, remember the people and provisions that have supported you this month.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Help you received, encouragement you needed, and goodness you want to pass along.

subject: Day 30: All 150—and a list worth keeping
title: Finish with praise, then save what you've gathered.
body:
Good morning.

The book ends with a chorus of praise. You've traveled through joy, anger, grief, confession, hope, and thanksgiving.

If you wrote three gratitudes each day, you now have 90. However many you recorded, take time to read them.

Date your list and keep it somewhere meaningful. Choose a few entries to read aloud with someone you love.

Give Thanks!
Heather
prompt: Something this journey helped you notice, a gift from this month, and a person you'd like to thank.
